kernel: the NAX (M5 tensor unit) prefill flash attention with a separate value head dim: MLX's steel_attention_nax kernel body (attention_nax_bdv) JIT-compiled per variant through mx.fast.metal_kernel, one threadgroup of four simdgroups covering BQ query rows x 32 keys per step with 16x16 fragments, an fp32 online softmax in the exp2 domain with per-head sinks as initial state, bottom-right aligned causal or bool masks, and key-range passes that hand the fp32 O/max/sum row state to the next dispatch
summary: Serves MiMo-V2 prefill attention on M5-class (NAX) hosts, where MLX 0.32.3 has no fused kernel for the 192 query/key / 128 value head-dim pair and its unfused fallback materialises the score matrix. Full-attention layers call it through mixed_head_dim_sdpa; sliding-window layers call it per 128-query block over block+window key spans through the caller-side blocked sliding-window path, consuming the strided key windows in place. Long contexts run as several 8192-key dispatches that resume the fp32 online-softmax state exactly, so split output is bit-identical to one dispatch.

models.name: MiMo-V2 / MiMo-V2-Flash
models.quant: bf16 activations, sinks and attention path; the checkpoint's MoE experts are MXFP4 (group 32, e8m0 scales) with fp8-dequantized dense parts, but the kernel only consumes bf16 or fp16 q/k/v
models.family: mimo_v2 (the mlx-lm patch, registered as both mimo_v2 and mimo_v2_flash)
models.machine: M5-class (NAX) hosts: macOS 26.2 or later, applegpu_g17 or later

settings.name: supported_head_dims
settings.condition: query/key head dim 192, value head dim 128; the only pair in SUPPORTED_HEAD_DIMS, any other pair returns None and the caller keeps its route

settings.name: query_tile_rows
settings.condition: one head-dim simdgroup (wn 1): BQ = WM * 16, four 16-row groups per threadgroup; the wn 2 head-dim-split kernel takes 32 (BQ = 16 * WM / WN)

settings.name: key_block_size
settings.condition: always (BK; each key block streams 32 keys per threadgroup step, two 16-key fragments)

settings.name: row_simdgroups
settings.condition: always (WM); wn 1: four 16-row groups, wn 2: two 16-row groups each split over two head-dim simdgroups

settings.name: threads_per_threadgroup
settings.condition: always (32 * WM); grid (NQ * 128, H, B) with threadgroup (128, 1, 1), one threadgroup per query tile per head per batch

settings.name: fragment_shape
settings.value: 16x16 tensor-op fragments, 8 elements per lane (2 rows x 4 columns, row jump 8)
settings.condition: always (kFragRows = kFragCols = 16, kElemsPerFrag = 256 / 32 = 8, in the nax_tiles.py port of MLX's steel nax.h)

settings.name: score_tile_fragments
settings.value: 1 x 2 (TQ x TK): 16 query rows x 32 keys per key block, two 16x16 output fragments accumulated per Q @ K.T fragment call
settings.condition: always (TK = BK / 16 = 2)

settings.name: output_tile_fragments
settings.value: 1 x TDV; TDV = BDV / 16 / WN = 8 at value head dim 128 wn 1 (16 rows x 128 value dims), 4 at wn 2
settings.condition: always; P @ V accumulates output fragments in pairs (TDV must be even)

settings.name: accumulator_dtype
settings.value: fp32 scores, fp32 O accumulator, fp32 running max and sum; stores round once to the activation dtype
settings.condition: always (AccumType = float in the generated instantiation)

settings.name: softmax_exp
settings.value: fast::exp2(x - y) (ExpSubOp); the rescale factor between key blocks is fast::exp2(max_score - new_max)
settings.condition: always (the whole softmax runs in the exp2 domain)

settings.name: scale_log2e_folding
settings.value: the attention scale is pre-multiplied by log2(e) = 1.44269504089 into one uniform multiplier applied to the raw scores
settings.condition: always

settings.name: sinks_init
settings.value: the per-head sink bias enters as initial softmax state: max_score = M_LOG2E_F * sink[h], sum_score = 1
settings.condition: has_sinks (sinks [H]; MiMo's attention_sink_bias per layer kind)

settings.name: additive_mask_scale
settings.value: a float mask adds M_LOG2E_F * mask to the exp2-domain score; a bool mask writes -inf (Limits::finite_min)
settings.condition: has_mask (the generated kernel handles bool or float MaskType; the Python gate only admits bool)

settings.name: causal_alignment
settings.value: bottom-right aligned: qL_off = kL - qL, so query row r attends to keys up to r + (kL - qL), matching MLX's causal mask
settings.condition: mask == "causal"

settings.name: causal_block_bounds
settings.value: per query tile: kb_lim = min(NK, ceil((tile end + qL_off) / BK)) and kb_min_causal = floor(tile start / BK); the elementwise r < c mask runs only for kb >= kb_min_causal, earlier blocks are fully visible
settings.condition: do_causal (this block bound is the kernel's causal work skip)

settings.name: row_max_reduction
settings.value: all of a row's score fragments reduced first, then simd_shuffle_xor 1 and 8 across lanes (max is exact, so the grouping is free)
settings.condition: every key block, before the exp2 rescale

settings.name: pass_keys
settings.condition: key-range passes; 0 would mean one dispatch. Grids of a wave or two (query tails under ~512 rows at 64 heads) keep one dispatch because their threadgroups stay in step anyway

settings.name: pass_min_threadgroups
settings.condition: B * H * ceil(qL / 64) below 512 keeps one dispatch

settings.name: pass_count
settings.value: n_pass = max(1, min(NK, round(NK * BK / pass_keys))), pass edges at (i * NK) / n_pass key blocks
settings.condition: only when the call clears pass_min_threadgroups and pass_keys > 0

settings.name: pass_state_row
settings.value: fp32 online-softmax row state of BDV + 2 = 130 floats per query row (O accumulator 128, running max, running sum), rows indexed [B, H, NQ * BQ]; the max and sum columns are written by lane sn 0 of d_part 0 only
settings.condition: key-range passes: non-first passes load it from Sin, non-last passes store it to Sout instead of normalising (bit-identical to one dispatch)

settings.name: pass_state_bytes
settings.value: B * H * NQ * BQ * (DV + 2) fp32 per call, about 3 GB at 128k keys, 8192 queries and 64 heads
settings.condition: passes in flight each hold their state until their command buffer ends

settings.name: dsplit_mode
settings.condition: 0 = never, 1 = for calls that run in key-range passes, 2 = always; WN = 2 splits the query/key and value dims over simdgroup pairs (MLX's attention_nax_dsplit scheme)

settings.name: dsplit_selection
settings.value: wn = 2 when mode == 2, or mode == 1 and the call has key-range passes (more than two pass edges); else wn = 1
settings.condition: per call

settings.name: dsplit_scratch_bytes
settings.value: WN 2: WM * 2 * 16 * 32 = 2048 fp32 (8192 bytes) of threadgroup exchange so the two simdgroups of a pair add their partial scores; WN 1: a 1-float placeholder
settings.condition: the wn 2 kernel only; the wn 1 kernel uses no threadgroup scratch

settings.name: pv_barrier_quirk
settings.value: at BDV 128 with WN 1, an extra simdgroup barrier sits inside the P @ V loop at output fragment pair id == 4
settings.condition: always for the (128 value dim, wn 1) variant (MLX's schedule, kept verbatim)

settings.name: output_layout
settings.value: [B, qL, H, DV] rows written directly, returned transposed as the [B, H, qL, DV] view implied by MLX's SDPA layout, so the caller's swapaxes and reshape stay views
settings.condition: always (the last pass only)

settings.name: stride_reads
settings.value: ensure_row_contiguous False: Q/K/V are read through their own strides (KV-cache slices, transposed projections, the blocked sliding-window key windows in place); only the head dim must be contiguous
settings.condition: always (no contiguity copies)

settings.name: kernel_variant_identity
settings.value: one mx.fast.metal_kernel per (dtype, BD, BDV, align_Q, align_K, has_mask, do_causal, has_sinks, FIRST, LAST, WN) variant, named omlx_nax_attention_v2_bd<bd>_bdv<bdv>_wn<wn>_<flag tag>, lru_cached per process
settings.condition: the MLX function constants (alignment, mask, causal, sinks) are template arguments of the generated source, so every combination is its own kernel

settings.name: self_check_tolerance
settings.value: max abs error < 2e-2 against an fp32 causal reference on q (1, 4, 100, 192), k (1, 2, 300, 192), v (1, 2, 300, 128) with unaligned query and key tails
settings.condition: one small case per process before first use; any exception or over-tolerance error disables the route for the process

settings.name: passes_bitexact_check
settings.value: the multi-pass output must equal the one-dispatch output bit for bit and stay within 2e-2 of fp32
settings.condition: first use of key-range passes per head-dim split; failure keeps long contexts on one dispatch

settings.name: sliding_window_query_block
settings.condition: blocked_sliding_window_attention block size (the same 128 is the padding hint window_query_padding offers callers)

settings.name: sliding_window_key_span
settings.value: block + window keys per query block, read as strided views of one contiguous KV copy (as_strided, stride block * D per block), so no per-block gather or reshape copy
settings.condition: the blocked sliding-window caller; the kernel itself just consumes the strided windows and the per-block band mask

gates.condition: NAX hardware, macOS half of the gate: macOS 26.2 or later (the Python fallback mirror of mlx metal::is_nax_available; the native extension answers instead when present)
NAX hardware, architecture half: applegpu_g17 or later; a trailing p suffix (g17p) requires g18 or later

is_nax_available = NAX hardware AND the installed mlx wheel's metallib carries the NAX kernels (the bytes 'affine_qmm_t_nax' in mlx.metallib); the JIT attention route checks this and is disabled when either half fails

mixed-dims route gate (mixed_head_dim_sdpa): qk_dim > v_dim, qL > 8, NAX available, qk_dim in (64, 72, 80, 96, 128, 192, 256), mask None or a string or a bool array; the JIT kernel is tried first when MLX's native fused kernel cannot take the pair or the call would run key-range passes

kernel dispatch gate (nax_mixed_head_dim_attention): 4-D inputs, (qk_dim, v_dim) == (192, 128), k_dim == qk_dim, bf16 or fp16 with all three dtypes equal, k/v shapes consistent with q, Hk > 0, H % Hk == 0, qL > 8, kL > 0; anything else returns None and the caller keeps its existing route
mask: None, the string 'causal', or a bool array broadcastable to (B, H, qL, kL); additive float masks are rejected
one-time self-check per process before first use (causal, unaligned tails, against fp32); a failure or over-tolerance error disables the route for the process
first use of key-range passes per head-dim split: several dispatches must equal one dispatch bit for bit and match fp32 within 2e-2, else the edges collapse to one dispatch and wn to 1
blocked sliding-window gate: B == 1, window > 0, prefix >= 0, L >= 2 * block (256), Lq equal to L or L padded to a whole block, keys and values the same length; mask 'causal' or a bool [..., L, S]

model-side prefill fast path (MiMo): L > 8 and the cache is not a quantized (bits) cache; sliding-window layers call blocked_sliding_window_attention with window = sliding_window_size and their sink bias, full layers mixed_head_dim_sdpa; a None result falls back to the masked full computation

measured.model: not model-specific (a comment about KV-head streaming)
measured.conditions: one dispatch over 1M keys runs at about 85 TFLOPS against about 103 TFLOPS with 8192-key passes at 64k context; the comment states why key-range passes exist (one long dispatch lets threadgroups drift apart until each re-streams its KV head from DRAM, per-slice dispatches keep the shared K/V on chip)
the head-dim split (WN 2) versus the single-simdgroup kernel on calls that run in key-range passes (long contexts); it changes only the fp32 summation order of Q @ K.T
elements whose last bf16 bit differs from the one-simdgroup kernel (the dsplit pair adds two 96-dim fp32 partial dot products)
fp32 online-softmax row state held by passes in flight until their command buffer ends, at 128k keys, 8192 queries, 64 heads

measured.machine: not named (the comparison motivates the blocked path on any GPU)
measured.conditions: MLX's array-mask sliding-window path at a 128-token window and 4K context: every query scores every key and the window only masks the result; the blocked path skips those key blocks

measured.model: mixed head-dim prefill on NAX GPUs
measured.conditions: padding V to the 192 query head dim lands on MLX's classic (non-NAX) kernel versus zero-padding Q/K/V to 256 for the NAX head-dim-split kernel; the comment is in mixed_head_dim_sdpa's route description

lab_mapping.maps_to: knobs.rs prefill_rows_attn (TURBOSPARK_PREFILL_ROWS_ATTN), our rows-per-prefill-attention-dispatch lever (qwen35, exactness KlBounded); ours toggles between batched row ops and per-row dispatch, theirs is a fixed 64-row (32-row dsplit) tensor-unit tile with 16-row fragment groups
lab_mapping.note: the natural first axis to sweep against this baseline when an M5-class host reaches the bench (our decision table defers all NAX kernels to that day)

lab_mapping.maps_to: none yet: the lab's kernel benches are attn_decode and int4_matmul only (crates/lab/src/kernel/mod.rs), there is no prefill attention bench and no key-range split axis
lab_mapping.note: the fp32 O/max/sum carry between key-range dispatches is the prefill analogue of the split-KV decode partials recorded in kapitsa.attn; a prefill arm would need that state plumbing first

lab_mapping.maps_to: none yet: crates/window-fit decides the conversation window, but there is no blocked sliding-window kernel or bench axis here
lab_mapping.note: omlx's block skip is caller-side (a blocked band mask plus strided key windows), not a kernel feature, so porting it is a host-side change like our window-fit

notes: Doc row (MLX_SERVE_KERNELS.md:145) versus source: the mechanism list (causal, sliding window with block skip, sinks, key-range passes with an fp32 carry) matches, with one ownership correction - the sliding-window block skip is not in the kernel. The kernel takes a bool mask; the block skip lives in the caller (blocked_sliding_window_attention, fast_attention.py), which tiles queries into 128-row blocks over block+window key spans and passes the per-block band mask; the kernel docstring only says the strided key windows of the blocked path are consumed in place. 'q/k 192 or 128': at this rev omlx validates only (192, 128) (SUPPORTED_HEAD_DIMS, nax_attention.py:64). A 128/128 sliding layer is not served by this JIT kernel; it runs MLX's own fused SDPA (head dim 128 is one of MLX's native NAX widths, 64/96/128/256/512 per the module docstring) under the block mask. The 'or 128' and 'Flint sliding layers' describe the mlx-serve port's extension: omlx has no Flint code on this path (Flint is imported from mlx_vlm at runtime, oq.py:4520, and nothing in omlx calls blocked_sliding_window_attention except the MiMo patch), so the only model served at this rev is MiMo-V2. Doc origin 'oMLX, from MLX steel_attention_nax.h' matches: the file header names mlx/backend/metal/kernels/steel/attn/kernels/steel_attention_nax.h (Apple, MIT) and states only the value head dim is separated, the kernel body is MLX's. The doc counts mlx-serve's port at 640 .metal lines; the omlx origin is a 1,026-line Python module whose Metal source is string literals compiled at runtime through mx.fast.metal_kernel plus the shared 852-line nax_tiles.py header (omlx's own port of MLX's steel attn/gemm nax.h), so there is no .metal file to pin in omlx. The hardware gate is stricter than our doc's one-line probe description: besides macOS 26.2+ and applegpu_g17+ (g17p needs g18+), omlx also requires the installed mlx wheel's metallib to contain the NAX kernels (the affine_qmm_t_nax needle), because a macOS < 26.2-built wheel stays on classic kernels on M5 hardware. Exactness claims, all canary-checked per process rather than assumed: single-dispatch output is bit-identical to MLX's native 192/128 kernel on builds that carry it (docstring, nax_attention.py:24); key-range passes reproduce one dispatch bit for bit because the fp32 row state resumes exactly, checked on first use; the dsplit (WN 2) variant differs in the last bf16 bit of ~0.5% of outputs and is therefore enabled by default only for pass calls. Every performance number is a code comment with no harness, no absolute times and no named chip; the kernel is coupled to the installed mlx build (pinned mlx==0.32.4 in pyproject) because it compiles through mx.fast.metal_kernel against that wheel. Coverage: this entry covers the JIT NAX prefill attention and its MiMo caller-side routing (mixed head dims, blocked sliding window); the QSA sparse and MLA NAX attention kernels are separate entries, and the classic-path decode SDPA is not covered.
